title: canResolveInflightOperation is classified as pure but its semantics imply domain-state coupling that is underspecified
description: canResolveInflightOperation(payjpState, memberState) is classified as pure (behavioral-spec.md line 35; verification-architecture.md line 39) with the verifiable property 'Integrity match'. However, neither artifact defines what constitutes an 'integrity match'. The function takes PayjpSubscriptionState and MemberState as inputs — types whose structure is not specified in the behavioral spec. Without knowing the fields of these types and the comparison logic, the function's purity cannot be properly verified. A pure function must have deterministic behavior that can be described without reference to external state, but 'integrity match' is too vague to serve as a property specification.
recommendation: Define the PayjpSubscriptionState and MemberState types in the behavioral spec (at minimum, their required fields). Specify the exact integrity comparison logic: which fields must match, and what constitutes a mismatch. Add a PROP-SYNC test that exercises the integrity match boundaries.
